proof_attempt_summary: D0 discharged the matched finite-sample root-risk and honest-length frontier min{1,(n*kappa)^(-1/2)+sqrt(K)/(n*kappa)}, consistency n*kappa/sqrt(K)->infinity, and strength-adaptive procedures. The stronger primary model removes overlap and cell floors, and explicit corollaries recover the original posed model; the typed math referee passed. Field-floor review capped the work at subfield (score 7<7.4) for substantive benchmark scope/calibration limitations; formalization was not entered.
tldr: For the population saturated-IV weighted LATE, the finite-sample minimax root mean squared error and minimax 95\% honest expected connected-interval length both have order \(\min\{1,(n\kappa)^{-1/2}+\sqrt K/(n\kappa)\}\), with universal two-sided constants. Both vanish exactly when \(n\kappa/\sqrt K\to\infty\). The explicit clipped collision ratio and one score-inversion interval retain every category and record, including unobserved and singleton labels. The interval is honest over every positive strength and simultaneously attains every shellwise length rate without knowing the shell, so adaptation has zero rate loss. The primary common-rank causal class enlarges the originally posed model by removing uptake overlap and the population four-cell floor. The two posed-model corollaries answer the original task exactly, with the same rates, constants, procedures, and consistency condition. Their lower comparisons use normalized causal witnesses with uptake in \([3/8,5/8]\) and cells at least \(5/32\). The separate published-class comparison transfers only converse bounds for an observed-law ratio, without an upper-frontier or ATE/WATE transfer.
gap: Yap \cite{yap2026manyweakheterogeneity} studies conditional JIVE score inference and already supplies a conservative small-group implementation. Zeng et al. \cite{zeng2026discretecovariates} supply categorical quadratic estimation and lower bounds for different causal functionals. The remaining question is their full-record support and strength counterpart for the population ratio \(\beta\), including unobserved categories and honest expected interval length.
fill: The kernel asks for a two-sided characterization of \(R\) and \(H\), with attaining all-category procedures and necessary and sufficient consistency conditions. The lower comparison must embed normalized common-rank causal alternatives and control their complete likelihood at every occupancy. Score inversion then tests whether shellwise precision can be attained by one interval across unknown positive strengths.
